_comment: Carry destination for issue #1067's remaining stage, W1067-G3 (the solver
half of the supply-temperature work). No roster group in this tree claims
#1067, so this file is that stage's brief. Shape and required fields:
stage: W1067-G3, the solver half of #1067: pricing the measured supply-temperature lift into the horizon behind its own flag

carries.from: W1067-G2, the learner half, whose own brief predicted that judging the efficiency reference against the measured lift would make the learned scale move less per sample
carries.control: The assumption invalidated: that a lift-aware efficiency REFERENCE slows cop_scale walking with the weather. It cannot. target_scale is cop_scale * commanded / measured, an expression the reference curve does not appear in, so no reference can move it. Measured on a 180-row grid (six outdoor temperatures x thirty consecutive folds) through the production _learn_measured_cop: a 55 degC supply reading against none separated zero rows of the cop_scale column. The null control ran the same grid at the merge base with no supply slot and diffed it byte for byte: identical.
carries.remeasure: Rebuild the grid at your own merge base: drive the production _learn_measured_cop through a shim carrying _flow_bias, once with observe_temps(55.0, 47.0) and once without, and diff the cop_scale column. Judge your own change on whether that column separates, because the learner half could not move it.
carries.brief: Pricing the lift is the only lever on cop_scale. The bias to apply is FlowCurveBias.bias_k in flow_lift.py, and the curve it was learned against is curve_supply_temp: call that function rather than re-deriving the curve, because a bias learned against one curve and spent against another is a silent offset. A bias with samples == 0 is exactly 0.0, and FlowCurveBias.from_dict enforces that on load, so it stays inert rather than being read as a measured zero. The bias is legitimate to spend only where the supply reading behind it was fresh and the interval space-dominant, which is what _fold_flow_lift gates on. The learner half ships no lift arithmetic: thermal_model.py is unchanged from main, and compute_cop's only lift is still the buffer term behind cop_flow_carnot. Fixtures: the learner half moved the five coordinator captures (six new heat_pump_signals keys each, all null or false) and config_flow, both claimed ADD-ONLY; every plan fixture is byte-identical. Yours will move solver fixtures, so claim that drift in tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt with its direction rather than re-recording it.

carries.from: W1067-G2 round 2 (#1068 review, comment 5703433010): the lift-aware reference double-counted the lift, and the owner chose to revert it (option 1)
carries.control: The model _learn_measured_cop holds is in its own comment: the heat the plan intended is commanded power times the modelled COP, and observed_cop = modelled_cop * commanded / measured. Under it the reference must be the COP the PLAN priced. A pump at supply S with true COP Ct = C0 * L(S) delivers the plan's heat at measured = commanded / L(S), and the ratio already carries the lift. Measured with the reviewer's lift_consistency.py (a pump generated from the model's own Carnot lift), at 8 degC outdoor and a 55 degC supply: the base credits 2.2285, the true COP, exactly. The lifted reference credited 1.3844, 37.9 % low (-24 to -38 % across -15..12 degC); the T4a residual read -2.2031 against -1.3590; and the envelope's thermal kW was 6.6856 against the true 10.7625. The null control at 35 degC, where L = 1, was identical in every column. tests/features.py pins the exact credit, 2.2285 mapped and unmapped.
carries.remeasure: Run lift_consistency.py (its source is in #1068's body and in comment 5703433010) at your merge base and your head, model 1, supplies 35 and 55, mapped and unmapped. Credited error must be 0 on every row at both ends, and the 35 degC rows identical. After pricing the lift, re-derive what the plan's COP is for a direct plant: if compute_cop then applies the curve-plus-bias lift, the reference follows that priced value automatically, because it is compute_cop(outdoor). Never feed it the measured supply.
carries.brief: Two constraints on the solver half. (1) The efficiency reference stays the COP the plan priced. When G3 prices the lift inside compute_cop, the reference inherits it. A second lift taken from the measured supply is the double count the review refuted. (2) The degradation watch (_observe_cop_health) is NOT lift-aware, and making it so is owed here, once the lift is priced. Measured on a healthy pump in one 3 degC bucket at 8 degC outdoor, supply 45 -> 55 degC: base and the shipped learner half show a +18.3 % false shortfall; feeding the watch observed_cop / L(S) while a fresh supply reading exists shows 0.0 %. But a normalised baseline fed ONE raw sample taken while the reading had lapsed shows +23.9 % (sample at 45 degC) or +37.9 % (at 55 degC): worse than doing nothing, and it drives the CUSUM on a compressor fault report. Two designs close that, each with a cost: (a) skip the watch when the supply slot is configured but has no fresh reading, which needs a configured-but-unreadable signal FlowCurveBias does not carry today, since last_supply_c is None for both unmapped and unreadable; (b) key normalised and raw samples into separate baselines, which changes the stored _cop_baseline key format and needs its migration. Either way there is a migration trap: every existing baseline is in RAW units, so the first normalised samples read as better than baseline until it re-anchors, which briefly masks a real decline. Whichever design ships must carry a measured stale-reading control: a lapsed reading must not produce a shortfall the healthy pump does not have.

carries.from: W1067-G3, the solver half (feat/1067-g3-flow-curve-cop): pricing the curve-plus-bias lift measured against the curve it prices from
carries.control: The model's weather curve sits below the 35 degC reference flow on the stock house, so the one-sided lift prices nothing there, and the bias clamp caps what it can price anywhere. Measured through ThermalModel.curve_flow_temp and ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor on the golden house (tests/golden.py house(), single zone, option on): curve 25.4 / 24.3 / 23.2 / 22.4 degC at -20 / -10 / 0 / 8 degC outdoor; lift factor at curve plus the full 15 K clamp 0.9266 / 0.9252 / 0.9247 / 0.9284, against 0.7809 / 0.7372 / 0.6777 / 0.6212 for a real 55 degC supply. With bias 0 and +5 K the priced COP equals the option-off COP exactly (tests/features.py pins it). Null control: on a house whose curve crosses the reference (3 kW pump, two 0.2 kW/K zones; 38.7 degC at -10 degC) the same option does price the lift, the plan's cost rises with the bias, and with the plant running at curve plus bias the learned cop_scale holds 1.0000 over 30 folds where the option off walks to 0.9417-0.9765.
carries.remeasure: Re-derive the curve temperatures and the clamp-edge lift factor at your own merge base with those two methods, on the golden house and on the owner's stored configuration, before claiming any gain. Drive the plant model of the #1068 reviewer's lift_consistency.py with the option on (the fixer's extension, lift_consistency_g3.py, is in the G3 pull request body): credited error must be 0 on every row, and the cop_scale column must hold at 1.0 only where the plant runs at the priced flow. Run it with the plant at 55 degC as the case that must stop walking.
carries.brief: What is legitimate next, and only under that control: either calibrate the weather curve itself against the measured supply, so that curve plus a small bias reaches the plant's real flow, or price the lift from the measured supply directly when a fresh reading exists. Refused without a new measurement: widening the 15 K bias clamp, whose bound is argued in flow_lift.py against probe errors, not against this ceiling. Either route must keep the efficiency reference equal to the COP the plan priced (the #1068 double count), keep compute_cop_dhw unlifted, keep batch parity with the scalar path, and keep the health watch's stale-reading control (a lapsed supply reading must add no shortfall a healthy pump does not have).
